questions.answer: Current public mana formula uses per-target ceiling and counts overkill; all three code references use clipped realDamage and per-target rounding. Critical rolls, Wheel/charm shares and healing extension behavior are traced separately.

canary.answer: Damage is clipped to target remainingHP before life/mana leech. Leech skips extension damage and condition-origin damage. Mana and life are deterministic when the bounded share is nonzero (no chance roll in these functions), use per-target lround and clamp to realDamage. Native/equipment skill + WheelDrainBody + damage extension shares are additive; Void/Vamp charms add tier*100bps; the total is clamped to uint16. Base critical roll is shared before target loop at1bps resolution; failed base roll can lead to an additional per-race LowBlow roll, with target-specific SavageBlow damage. This is an explicit OTS algorithm, divergent from the current Mana ceiling/overkill reference. Ordinary applyExtensions early-returns for COMBAT_HEALING. The inspected BlessingOfTheGrove healing path boosts healing but has no corresponding critical roll in this function.

canary.answer: On refreshing existing paralysis, boots determine max recovery chance and OR pvpDeflect. With a player attacker, pvpDeflect reflects the incoming condition clone BEFORE the recovery RNG unless attacker boots also deflect (owner reset0 avoids ping-pong). It then rolls15/25/50 recovery. If recovery fails, the helper returns true only for pvpDeflect plus a player attacker, suppressing that PvP refresh; it otherwise returns false and permits normal refresh (including failed PvE recovery). No stored successful-gate lifetime exists in this inspected path. Reflection and the PvP suppression without a prior-success state predicate differ from the qualified Global reference; engine comments are not source proof.
